column2: σ(w·a + b): a weighted sum of its inputs plus a bias, squashed by a switch such as the sigmoid.
σ(z) = 1 / (1 + e^−z). It maps any number into the range 0 to 1.

column1: How many parameters does a 784-16-16-10 network have?
What does a first-layer neuron's weight picture show?
column2: Its 784 weights laid out as an image. They look messy, not like neat strokes: the network finds its own features.

column1: Where is the perceptron inside a transformer?
column2: The MLP in every block: 64 → 256 → 64 here, with GELU instead of the sigmoid.
Reusing the embedding table as the output layer. It is why GPT-2 small is 124 million parameters, not 163 million.

column1: Doubling the vector width does what to a block's parameters?
column2: Roughly quadruples them, because every matrix is width × width. Doubling the number of blocks only doubles them.

column1: Do more attention heads add parameters?
column2: No. Heads split the same Q, K and V matrices into slices.
Storing each parameter in fewer bits (16, 8, 4) so a model needs less memory.

column1: Roughly how much compute does training take?

column2: Low-Rank Adaptation: freeze W and learn a small correction B·A (rank r), so W·x becomes W·x + (α/r)·B·A·x. Here 8,192 trainable numbers instead of 153,344.

column1: Why does a merged LoRA adapter cost nothing at inference?
column2: B·A is folded back into W after training, so the model has exactly the same shape and speed as before.

column1: Does LoRA automatically forget less than full fine-tuning?
column2: No. Without replay, LoRA at its usual higher learning rate wrecked refusals (80% → 0%). Replay protected old skills more than the choice of method did.

column1: What does 4-bit quantization cost this model?
column2: About 7× smaller file, loss on unseen text up by about 0.012, the 45-question test unchanged.

column1: What is the alignment tax found here?
column2: Chat fine-tuning raised the loss on ordinary text from 0.37 to 5.15: the model lost its ability to predict plain text.
